item.title: When founders lose control: Tech leaders pushed out of their companies
item.description: Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit joins a list of high-profile departures involving boardroom battles and investor pressure ...
item.dc:creator: Barkha Mathur
item.content:encoded: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden resignation last week as chief executive is a reminder that founding a successful technology company does not necessarily guarantee its creator lasting control over its leadership. Over the years, some of the industry's most prominent entrepreneurs, including Steve Jobs, Travis Kalanick and Sam Altman, have left companies they helped build following disagreements with boards, investors or fellow executives. What led to these exits? 1. Jensen Huang: NvidiaYear of exit: 2026Reason: Resignation following controversy and a board investigation. Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. The semiconductor company has since become a major supplier of chips and computing infrastructure for artificial intelligence. Huang resigned as president and CEO on November 12, 2026, following reports of alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence of having links to China. Nvidia's board had initiated an independent investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The company did not specify the reason for his resignation. CFO Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO, while the board 2. Sam Altman: OpenAIYear of exit: 2023, returned within daysReason: Breakdown in trust between the chief executive and the board. Sam Altman co-founded OpenAI in 2015 and became its CEO in 2019. He led the organisation through the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022. On November 17, 2023, OpenAI's board removed Altman, saying he had not been consistently candid in his communications with directors. Co-founder Greg Brockman also stepped down as chairman. The decision triggered an employee backlash. Microsoft, OpenAI's major investor and partner, offered Altman a role leading a new AI research team if he did not return. On November 22, OpenAI announced his reinstatement under a reconstituted board. A subsequent independent review found that the removal followed a breakdown in trust between Altman and the previous board. 3. Adam Neumann: WeWorkYear of exit: 2019Reason: Governance concerns and mounting losses. Adam Neumann co-founded flexible workspace company WeWork in 2010 with Miguel McKelvey. The company's proposed IPO in 2019 exposed mounting losses and governance concerns, including questions about Neumann's management practices and transactions involving entities connected to him. WeWork reported a net loss of approximately $1.6 billion in 2018, against revenue of around $1.8 billion. The IPO was subsequently withdrawn amid investor concerns. On September 24, 2019, Neumann stepped down as CEO, with Artie Minson and Sebastian Gunningham taking over as co-CEOs. He initially remained non-executive chairman but left the board the following month. 4. Travis Kalanick: UberYear of exit: 2017Reason: Workplace culture controversies, management concerns and investor pressure. Travis Kalanick co-founded Uber in 2009 and helped turn it into a global ride-hailing platform. However, the company faced mounting criticism in 2017 over its workplace culture and management practices. A public account by former engineer Susan Fowler alleging sexual harassment and discrimination triggered an investigation into the company's workplace practices. The crisis escalated when five major investors, including venture capital firm Benchmark, demanded Kalanick's resignation in June 2017. He stepped down as CEO on June 20. Dara Khosrowshahi, then CEO of Expedia, succeeded him in August. 5. Andrew Mason: GrouponYear of exit: 2013Reason: Weakening business performance, falling share price and missed financial expectations. Andrew Mason co-founded Groupon in 2008, popularising the daily-deals model through discounts on products and services. The company went public in November 2011 but subsequently struggled with competition, slowing demand and concerns over its business model. The pressure intensified in February 2013, when Groupon reported disappointing quarterly results and issued revenue guidance below market expectations. On February 28, 2013, the board terminated Mason as CEO with immediate effect. He also resigned from the board. Executive chairman Eric Lefkofsky and vice-chairman Ted Leonsis took over as interim leaders. 6. Jack Dorsey: TwitterYear of exit: 2008Reason: Concerns over management style and the company's leadership. Jack Dorsey co-founded Twitter in 2006 with Biz Stone, Evan Williams and Noah Glass. He was its first CEO but was replaced by co-founder Evan Williams in October 2008 as the company expanded. Dorsey moved into the role of chairman and remained on the board. He returned as CEO in 2015, replacing Dick Costolo, but stepped down again in November 2021. Parag Agrawal succeeded him. His first departure was a board-led leadership change, while his second was officially announced as his own decision. 7. Jerry Yang: YahooYear of exit: 2008Reason: Shareholder pressure Jerry Yang co-founded Yahoo in 1994 with David Filo and became its CEO in June 2007. His tenure came under pressure in 2008 after Yahoo rejected Microsoft's $44.6 billion acquisition offer. The two companies failed to agree on a valuation, prompting criticism from shareholders who believed Yahoo had turned down a lucrative deal. Billionaire investor Carl Icahn launched a proxy battle to replace Yahoo's board and revive the negotiations. Amid mounting pressure and weakening business performance, Yahoo announced in November 2008 that it would look for a new CEO. Carol Bartz succeeded Yang in January 2009. 8. Martin Eberhard: TeslaYear of exit: 2007Reason: Disagreements over management, rising costs and production delays. Martin Eberhard co-founded Tesla Motors in 2003 with Marc Tarpenning. He served as its first CEO and led the development of the Roadster, the company's first electric car. However, the project faced engineering challenges, cost overruns and production delays. Tensions also emerged between Eberhard and Elon Musk, who had invested in Tesla in 2004 and become its chairman. In August 2007, Eberhard stepped down as CEO following a board decision. Michael Marks became interim CEO, followed by Ze'ev Drori. Eberhard subsequently left the company and became involved in a legal dispute with Musk over Tesla's founding and his departure. The dispute was settled in 2009, with five individuals recognised as Tesla co-founders. 9. Elon Musk: X.com and PayPalYear of exit: 2000Reason: Disagreements over technology, management and strategy. Elon Musk founded online financial services company X.com in 1999. It merged with Confinity in 2000, creating the business that eventually became PayPal. Musk initially served as CEO of X.com and subsequently led the merged company. However, disagreements emerged between Musk and other executives over its technology platform, branding and management. During a leadership challenge in September 2000, the board replaced Musk with co-founder Peter Thiel as CEO. Musk remained a shareholder. When eBay acquired PayPal in 2002 for approximately $1.5 billion, his stake generated substantial proceeds. 10. Steve Jobs: AppleYear of exit: 1985Reason: Boardroom power struggle and disagreements over management and strategy. Steve Jobs co-founded Apple in 1976 with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne. By the mid-1980s, disagreements had emerged between Jobs and then CEO John Sculley over the company's management and direction. In May 1985, an organisational restructuring stripped Jobs of his operational responsibilities. The board backed Sculley, prompting Jobs to resign from Apple later that year. He went on to establish computer company NeXT. Apple acquired NeXT in 1996, bringing Jobs back to the company in 1997. He subsequently became CEO and led Apple's transformation through products such as the iMac, iPod and iPhone.

item.title: Popular websites subverted in bid to steal crypto, target iPhone users
item.description: Malicious scripts delivered through website optimisation platform Optimizely attempted to steal payment details, cookies and screenshots, and install exploit code on iPhones ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Some of the world's most visited websites, including those belonging to Zoom, HSBC , Equifax, CNN, Salesforce and IKEA, were subverted in an effort to steal cryptocurrency and infect iPhones, a security researcher said on Monday. Malicious JavaScript was aimed at visitors to the websites of 178 organizations across various sectors through Optimizely, a website optimization platform, according to researcher Scott Helme. The scripts attempted to replace cryptocurrency payment addresses with the attacker's wallet, skim card numbers as users entered credit card details, steal cookies and screenshots, and plant exploit code on iOS devices. Cybersecurity firm HudsonRock also said it had found evidence that the sites had served malicious code to their visitors.Reuters could not immediately ascertain whether the code was successfully used in each case, or the extent of any resulting hacks. Salesforce said it was investigating unauthorized Optimizely script changes, and had disabled them as a precaution.Optimizely, Apple, Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN and IKEA did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

item.description: September-quarter net profit rose 19-27 per cent, estimates from six brokerages showed, as metals, energy, banks and industrials drove earnings growth and lifted market sentiment ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / India Inc logs best quarterly profit growth in 4 years, lifts market hopes

India Inc logs best quarterly profit growth in 4 years, lifts market hopes September-quarter net profit rose 19-27 per cent, estimates from six brokerages showed, as metals, energy, banks and industrials drove earnings growth and lifted market sentiment

Metals, oil and gas, banks, non-bank lenders and industrials did much of the heavy lifting, benefiting from higher commodity prices, stronger volumes, healthy credit growth and robust order books | Illustration: Ajay Mohanty

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 17 2026 | 2:14 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's top 50 firms posted their strongest profit growth in more than four years in the September quarter, driven by a broad-based recovery, estimates from six brokerages showed, strengthening the case for a return to equities. Net profit for companies part of the benchmark Nifty 50 index grew between 19 per cent and 27 per cent, with results broadly beating expectations, demonstrating greater resilience to cost pressures than investors had feared. Motilal Oswal called it a quarter of "earnings in full flight". This, along with a revival in foreign inflows and easing oil concerns, has brought optimism back into the equity market. The Nifty has climbed 12.2 per cent so far in the December quarter, putting it on course for its strongest quarterly performance in six years.

Metals, oil and gas, banks, non-bank lenders and industrials did much of the heavy lifting, benefiting from higher commodity prices, stronger volumes, healthy credit growth and robust order books. Cyclicals "led the pack", BofA said. The brokerage, along with Morgan Stanley, identified metals, energy, utilities and industrials as generating the biggest upside to estimates. Also Read

Punjab National Bank share price zooms 31% in 1 month; hits 8-year high

Kaynes Tech falls 16% in 2 sessions; Jefferies flags margin pressure

Oil seen at $78 by 2027 amid supply glut expectation: Mirae Asset Sharekhan

Brainbees snaps 3-day losing run, jumps 13%; JM Fin says worst over post Q2

Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI), metals, oil and gas, and automobiles together accounted for 77 per cent of incremental profit growth, said Motilal Oswal. Revenue growth kept pace with the strong earnings showing. PhillipCapital estimated Nifty revenue growth at 22 per cent, while Emkay put sales growth excluding financials at 24.6 per cent.

The stronger showing has prompted some analysts to nudge up earnings forecasts, though not dramatically. Motilal Oswal raised its fiscal 2027 Nifty earnings per share estimate by 0.9 per cent and fiscal 2028 by 1.4 per cent, while Emkay kept its forecasts largely unchanged. However, the recovery was not quite a rising tide lifting all boats. Despite the resilience in corporate earnings, pockets of margin pressure persisted as higher raw-material, energy, freight and logistics costs outpaced price increases in several sectors. The strain was most visible in consumer-facing businesses, where pricing power was uneven, as well as cement, chemicals and capital goods, where elevated fuel, commodity and project-input costs squeezed profitability.

JSW Steel, Tata Steel, Larsen & Toubro, Dr Reddy's and Titan featured among notable positive surprises while Tata Motors, Eternal, Sun Pharma and Bharti Airtel were among the key disappointments.

item.title: Xi, Carney seek closer China-Canada ties amid strained US relations
item.description: The leaders of China and Canada called for deeper ties Tuesday as Ottawa navigates strained relations with the United States and seeks closer cooperation with Beijing.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Xi, Carney seek closer China-Canada ties amid strained US relations

Xi, Carney seek closer China-Canada ties amid strained US relations The leaders met ahead of the APEC summit, a day after Canada's prime minister said Ottawa could turn to Chinese automakers if trade talks with Donald Trump fail

Delegations led by Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney attend a bilateral meeting | Image Credit: Reuters

AP Shenzhen 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 17 2026 | 1:16 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The leaders of China and Canada called for deeper ties Tuesday as Ottawa navigates strained relations with the United States and seeks closer cooperation with Beijing. Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' summit, and both praised the strategic partnership they agreed to pursue this year and pointed to improving economic ties. The meeting came a day after Carney said Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with US President Donald Trump fail to maintain an integrated North American auto industry. "Improving and developing China-Canada relations serves the interests of the people of both countries and is also conducive to safeguarding world peace, stability, development and prosperity," said Xi. "This is the right choice."   Carney said that the exchanges between Canada and China have increased in the past months and praised that now there is "greater predictability and stability" in their relationship.

"The stabilisation of our bilateral trade arrangement is indicative of how we can work together more broadly, pragmatically, to solve problems," he said. Xi and Carney reached an agreement in January allowing tens of thousands of Chinese electric vehicles into Canada at reduced tariffs. Under the January agreement, Canada reduced its 100 per cent tariff on Chinese electric vehicles to 6.1 per cent, initially allowing up to 49,000 vehicles annually, with the cap increasing over time. In exchange, China agreed to lower tariffs on Canadian agricultural products, including canola.
